title: goalforge stage.report payload
description: The PAYLOAD of a stage.report trace event (spec.md C6). This file is the ONLY seam goalforge-viz consumes (ticket-76). The trace ENVELOPE that carries this payload is the schema embedded in references/trace-events.md; the two documents agree field for field on the payload (wp-07 b5) and a fork between them is a test failure, not a variant. The `ref` pattern `^[^\s:]+(:[0-9]+|#[^\s].*)$` is written out at each site rather than factored into `definitions` + `$ref`: the only validator in this package (goalforge-trace-emit `_validate`) implements a draft-07 SUBSET with no `$ref` resolution, so a factored pattern would silently never be applied.

stage.description: The C7-touchpoint-owning stage that emitted this report.

wp.description: WP id, or the feature id for a feature-level touchpoint (capture, spec).

reader.description: Reader slug per C8. The local-part of an address at most — the full email is never stored, and this pattern admits no `@`.

changed.description: What this stage changed since the reader last saw it.

issues.description: One entry per thing the reader must decide or know. Zero issues is legal (a clean gate); every issue present carries a `ref`.

id.description: Stable id (WP slug, ticket id, decision id). Required for an issue that may later land in `assumed_known[]`, and named in the overflow line when the issue collapses.

evidence.description: Optional quoted evidence. The LOCATOR for that evidence is `ref`, which is what C6 requires of every issue.

options.description: A genuine choice, so at least two entries when present.

next_gate.description: The ask this touchpoint puts to the reader. Never collapsed by the overflow rule and never suppressed by `assumed_known` (wp-07 OQ1, C7).

assumed_known.description: Ids the reader profile marks seen; the report names them and omits their body.
